answer: In an agent market trading nectar and opal from farms along a ridge, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents yields the same total voting power as one agent holding 100 tokens. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, bearing their purchase cost, price risk, and lost use during the lock.
